policy: final person-name policy (2026-10-23): clearly identifiable person names are FIRSTNAME/LASTNAME targets regardless of public-figure status; no celebrity whitelist
note: challenge_v1.txt itself is frozen and unchanged. Its original annotations treated public figures as negatives (!PUBLICNAME), which contradicts the final policy. This overlay produces the derived set 'challenge_v1_policy'. Results are reported for BOTH. challenge_v1 has been inspected after round 1 and is a regression/debugging set only, not an unbiased benchmark.

neg-027.reason: real persons; a mononym has no defined FIRSTNAME/LASTNAME type, so it is ignored at entity level (the document is BLOCK via the other name)

neg-012.reason: fictional characters: person-name-shaped but not persons; the policy does not decide them, so the document is ambiguous and excluded from document metrics

unchanged_but_documented.code-013: AWS secret access key, annotated ~SECRET (ignored). API keys are outside the 13-label scope. The document is ambiguous: a detector is neither required nor penalised for blocking it.
unchanged_but_documented.chat-033: CVV with descriptive cue ('the 3 digits on the back') and a trailing cue ('security code'): sufficient evidence under the v3 CVV rule, so it remains a genuine positive.
